title: Preferences: choose a cadence; consent is never assumed
description:
The reader's preferences page shows each family as one choice (every new item, daily summary, off) and each newsletter as a tick. Changing cadence inside a family the reader already consented to needs no new confirmation; joining a new family or newsletter does. A reader is never enrolled in a list by a migration or a new feature: a new list starts empty. Consent evidence (wording, time, form) is stored per family.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A new list has no members until readers choose it.
- Switching cadence keeps consent; a new family asks for it.
- Unsubscribe from one message removes that list only; 'unsubscribe from everything' removes all.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- subscription-preferences.feature: a new daily list starts empty; a weekly subscriber is not added to it; switching every-item to daily needs no new opt-in; joining a new family sends a confirmation; one-click unsubscribe is honoured before the next send.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** Caducus and the notifications plugin pages.

**Part of:** Newsletters and subscriptions: weekly, daily and every new item. Slice code N7 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
